title: Where can I find 3D enemies like these?
author: Aromatic_Dig_5631
selftext:
Hey,

for my next game I wanna create a Serious Sam clone but in a magical dungeon world. This image was created with Nano Banana. I really like the artstyle of these enemies. But I couldnt find something like this in the Unity Asset Store. 

Anyone got an idea where I can find 3D models like those enemies?

comments.author: FailedGradAdmissions
comments.body:
Get into illustrator, clip the enemies, then back into nano banana to retouch it, then use one of the tons of image to 3D assets.

Then retouch it on Blender, as most if not all image to 3D pipelines are great at build in the model, but they use too many polygons and performance is trash.

replies.body: Just look up Blender Face Animation tutorial, there’s 15 minute tutorials that teach you all you’ll need for simple face animations.

replies.author: Aromatic_Dig_5631
replies.body: I dont understand anything but would it look exactly like in this image? All the colors and outlines?

replies.author: erofamiliar
replies.body: So, if something has an outline, it's either a shader (which AI won't automatically do) or it's an inverse hull thing (which the AI also won't automatically do). Just knowing the terms will help you find tutorials on how to do it in whatever engine you're shooting for

comments.author: Icy-Swordfish7784
comments.body:
Hunyuan studio lets you generate meshes and reduce them to a game ready polycount with proper UV maps and can also rig the model for animation.

[Tencent Hunyuan 3D](https://3d.hunyuan.tencent.com/)

comments.author: Still_Ad9431
comments.body: text to image with Leonardo AI then generate image to 3d with Tripo

replies.author: Aromatic_Dig_5631
replies.body: I was searching for hours and couldnt find any. I need that real anime look. Do you know of an asset like that? Would be great if I could just buy some and dont do them myself.

replies.author: Such_Neck_644
replies.body: Just look for cell shading monsters.

comments.author: ZenCyberDad
comments.body: The art style is called Cell Shading, basically a black outline around the model to make it look like a cartoon

replies.author: Renusek
replies.body: Cel* shading. And no, it's not basically a black outline, it has to do with lighting, the colors are flat and don't have a gradient.

comments.author: Dany_GeminiDev
comments.body: Get Nano Banano to make a copy of one of those on a black background, then run it through Hyper 3D Rodin AI to create the 3D model, and then into Blender to tweak the textures and add bones.
